subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-year-old girl is brought for progressive clumsiness and frequent falls over 8 months; her parents report declining speech and attention. Examination shows ataxia, hyperreflexia, and extensor plantar responses, and brain MRI shows diffuse white matter demyelination.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Progressive ataxia, cognitive decline, and diffuse white matter demyelination in a young child suggest metachromatic leukodystrophy. Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes cerebroside sulfate (sulfatide) to accumulate in oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells, producing central and peripheral demyelination. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

explanation_incorrect.B: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes Krabbe disease, which produces globoid cells from psychosine toxicity.
explanation_incorrect.C: Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease, an X-linked disorder with angiokeratomas and painful neuropathy.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease with a cherry-red spot and early neuronal death.
explanation_incorrect.E: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease with hepatosplenomegaly and pancytopenia.

educationalObjective: Metachromatic leukodystrophy results from arylsulfatase A deficiency, with cerebroside sulfate accumulation and central and peripheral demyelination.
